title: Cyclic Vector Theorem: Full Biconditional
description: Proves the converse direction of the cyclic vector theorem: if M has a cyclic vector then M is nonderogatory (minpoly = charpoly). Combined with the parent theorem (nonderogatory → cyclic vector), this gives the full biconditional: IsNonderogatory M ↔ ∃ v, IsCyclicVector M v. Fully machine-verified: 0 sorries, 0 axioms.

meta.author: Lean Genius Research
meta.assumptions: No axioms or sorries. Uses only Mathlib's Polynomial and Matrix APIs.
originalContributions: cyclic_implies_nonderogatory: proves the converse direction — if M has a cyclic vector v then minpoly K M = M.charpoly
nonderogatory_iff_has_cyclic_vector: full biconditional combining parent and converse directions
derogatory_has_no_cyclic_vector: contrapositive — a derogatory matrix has no cyclic vector
minpoly_natDegree_of_cyclic: degree characterization — a matrix with a cyclic vector has deg(minpoly) = n
meta.historicalContext: The cyclic vector theorem is a cornerstone of rational canonical form theory. The forward direction (nonderogatory → cyclic vector) was proved in the parent entry using primary decomposition over arbitrary fields. The converse direction settled here completes the characterization: a matrix is nonderogatory if and only if it has a cyclic vector. This biconditional is the key step in showing that every nonderogatory matrix is similar to its companion matrix.
meta.proofStrategy: Given a cyclic vector v for M, we show deg(minpoly K M) = n by a degree squeeze: (1) minpoly | charpoly via Cayley-Hamilton, giving deg ≤ n; (2) if deg < n, the cyclic condition forces minpoly = 0, contradicting ne_zero, giving deg ≥ n. Then both minpoly and charpoly are monic of the same degree with minpoly | charpoly, forcing equality.

overview.problemStatement:
**Open question from cayley-hamilton-cyclic-vector-all-fields**: Is the cyclic vector theorem an equivalence? The parent theorem shows every nonderogatory matrix has a cyclic vector. Does the converse hold — if M has a cyclic vector, must M be nonderogatory?

More precisely: does
$$\text{IsNonderogatory}(M) \iff \exists v,\, \text{IsCyclicVector}(M, v)$$
hold over any field?
overview.historicalContext: A matrix M is nonderogatory if its minimal polynomial equals its characteristic polynomial. The cyclic vector theorem states that every nonderogatory matrix has a cyclic vector — a vector v such that {v, Mv, ..., M^(n-1)v} is a basis. The converse is also classical: if v is cyclic for M, then the map p(M)v gives a module isomorphism K[X]/(minpoly) ≅ K^n, forcing minpoly = charpoly. This formalization completes the biconditional by providing the Lean proof of the converse.
keyInsights: A cyclic vector forces deg(minpoly) ≥ n: if deg < n, the cyclic condition (IsCyclicVector M v) requires minpoly(M)·v ≠ 0 for any nonzero p with deg(p) < n — but minpoly(M) = 0 as a matrix, giving a contradiction.
Both minpoly and charpoly are monic of degree n with minpoly | charpoly. Extracting the quotient r = charpoly / minpoly and using degree arithmetic shows deg(r) = 0, forcing r = 1.
The final step uses Polynomial.Monic.of_mul_monic_left to deduce that r is monic, then eq_C_of_natDegree_eq_zero to write r = C(r.coeff 0) = C(1) = 1.
The biconditional nonderogatory_iff_has_cyclic_vector trivially combines cyclic_implies_nonderogatory with nonderogatory_has_cyclic_vector from the parent entry.
overview.proofStrategy:
**Step 1 (deg ≤ n)**: minpoly K M divides M.charpoly by Cayley-Hamilton (minpoly.dvd), so natDegree(minpoly) ≤ natDegree(charpoly) = n.

**Step 2 (deg ≥ n)**: Suppose natDegree(minpoly) < n. Then aeval M (minpoly K M) = 0 (as a matrix), so (aeval M (minpoly K M)).mulVec v = 0. But IsCyclicVector M v requires this to be nonzero for any nonzero annihilator with degree < n — contradiction since minpoly ≠ 0.

**Step 3 (equality)**: natDegree(minpoly) = n. Write charpoly = minpoly · r. Both sides monic of degree n: deg(r) = 0, r monic, so r = 1 and charpoly = minpoly.
prerequisites: minpoly.dvd: the minimal polynomial divides any annihilating polynomial (applied to Cayley-Hamilton)
minpoly.aeval: aeval M (minpoly K M) = 0 as a matrix
Polynomial.Monic.of_mul_monic_left: if p·q is monic and p is monic, then q is monic
Polynomial.eq_C_of_natDegree_eq_zero: a polynomial of degree 0 equals C(coeff 0)
openQuestions: Does the biconditional extend to matrices over commutative rings (not just fields)? The proof crucially uses that K[X] is a PID to extract the quotient r.
Can the converse be used to give a shorter proof of the rational canonical form theorem? The biconditional shows nonderogatory matrices are 'as good as' companion matrices.

sections.title: Main Converse: Cyclic Vector Implies Nonderogatory
sections.content: If M has a cyclic vector v, then M is nonderogatory (minpoly K M = M.charpoly). The proof squeezes the degree of the minimal polynomial from both sides: divisibility by charpoly gives deg ≤ n, and the cyclic condition forces deg ≥ n. With both polynomials monic of degree n and one dividing the other, they must be equal.

sections.title: Full Biconditional
sections.content: Combining the converse proved here with the forward direction from the parent entry (CayleyHamiltonCyclicVectorAllFields), we obtain the full biconditional: a matrix over any field is nonderogatory if and only if it has a cyclic vector.

sections.title: Corollaries
sections.content: The contrapositive gives that derogatory matrices have no cyclic vector. The degree characterization shows any matrix with a cyclic vector has natDegree(minpoly) = n.

conclusion.summary: The full biconditional IsNonderogatory M ↔ ∃ v, IsCyclicVector M v is now machine-verified over arbitrary fields in Lean 4. The converse direction proves that a cyclic vector forces the minimal polynomial to have degree n, completing the characterization of nonderogatory matrices.
conclusion.significance: This completes the cyclic vector characterization of nonderogatory matrices in Mathlib-compatible Lean 4. The biconditional is the key step connecting nonderogatory matrices to companion matrices in rational canonical form theory.
openProblems: Extend to modules over commutative Noetherian rings (not just fields)
Use the biconditional to give a shorter RCF existence proof
